corrections: C1 asql-window-ranking analogy: "dead heat" yet "finish-line camera still lists one of them first" (self-contradictory: a dead heat is declared because the photo cannot separate them) -> results printout must put one name above the other; limit reworded (printer may choose a rule; ROW_NUMBER none) + convention-varies note.
C2 asql-conditional-pivots: per-customer month-count table listed Ana, Dev, Eve only (Ben and Cat silently omitted from a 5-customer result) -> added Ben 1/0/1 and Cat 0/1/1 (executed SQLite 3.51).

C3 asql-relational-division: author moved the COUNT vs COUNT(DISTINCT) pitfall (Ana counted 3 and excluded; Kettle-twice-no-Mug wrongly passes) inside the collapsed analogy's 'Where it stops', hiding a fact that question asql-interview-problems-q4 tests -> restored as visible prose after the callout.

C4 asql-median-rows: "part of the SQLite source from 3.51.0 ... the macOS 3.51.0 CLI had it" misattributed why the CLI works: the sqlite3 CLI has bundled median()/percentile*() since 3.47.0 (changes.html), whereas the library amalgamation includes it from 3.51.0 only with SQLITE_ENABLE_PERCENTILE (and before that it was in the source tree as a separately compiled loadable extension, so "part of the source from 3.51.0" was wrong). macOS /usr/bin/sqlite3 PRAGMA compile_options has no ENABLE_PERCENTILE yet median() works. Reworded; also noted SQLite's percentile_cont(total, 0.5) spelling (no WITHIN GROUP without SQLITE_ENABLE_ORDERED_SET_AGGREGATES).
C5 glossary sqlite-percentile-extension: same "included in the SQLite source from 3.51.0" error -> amalgamation from 3.51.0 behind SQLITE_ENABLE_PERCENTILE; CLI since 3.47.0. Example reworded.

C6 asql-json-storage analogy limit: 'jsonb ... discards only presentation details such as whitespace, key order and duplicate keys' overstated fidelity (executed PG 18.6: '1.230e-5' -> 0.00001230, 'é' -> é) and called dropped duplicate keys presentation -> values kept but spelling may be rewritten; original text (whitespace, key order, earlier duplicate keys) not kept.

C7 asql-atomic-upserts analogy limit: 'waits ... until the first transaction commits or rolls back' implied the waiter then always succeeds; two-session test on PG 18.6 (race.sh/race.out): same-key waits on transactionid lock (new and existing key, DO UPDATE and DO NOTHING), different key does not wait; after commit READ COMMITTED takes the update path (2 -> 12, 1 -> 17) but REPEATABLE READ fails 'could not serialize access due to concurrent update' -> limit now states both outcomes.

C8 asql-upsert-batch-replace: author moved the REPLACE side effects (delete triggers only with recursive_triggers, ON DELETE CASCADE removes child rows) and the 'use DO UPDATE' advice from visible prose into the collapsed analogy limit; question asql-json-upsert-q5's workedExample relies on them -> restored as visible prose after the callout (executed SQLite 3.51/3.53: child row cascaded, trigger logged only with PRAGMA recursive_triggers=ON).

C9 glossary wrong-sense links in new author prose: exists-null-trap analogy "rule of three-valued logic" opened software-engineering 'rule-of-three' -> "fixed rules of SQL's three-valued logic"; correlated-subqueries analogy (x2) and quantified-comparisons "outer row" opened databases/04 join outer/inner side -> "row of the outer query". (My own new upsert text: "serialization error" would open system-design entry -> "serialization failure", this module's own entry.)

C10 pre-existing wrong-sense cross-subject links reworded in this module: 'request deduplication' (atomic-upserts intro) opened React request-sharing -> 'must recognise and skip a repeated request'; 'error handling' (merge-concurrency) opened JavaScript try...catch -> 'raise errors that the application must handle or retry'. analogyReview.scope: All 41 active lessons: 19 analogies added by the authors (5 by cf2-dbs-advanced-author, 14 by cf2-dbs-advanced-author2) reviewed for scenario, mapping, limit, visibility of required facts and glossary links inside the callout; 22 lessons reviewed and recorded as not needing one.

asql-scalar-subqueries.rationale: Fixture and definitional unit; the shapes table and executed examples are clearer than a comparison.

asql-membership-derived-tables.rationale: The semi-join point is made by a concrete executed join-versus-IN contrast; an analogy would repeat it.

asql-correlated-subqueries.rationale: Pupil list = outer query, 'this pupil's class' = the correlated predicate; limit (no promised method; unqualified names bind to the nearest table) is accurate. Two 'outer row' links to the databases/04 join entry reworded.

asql-exists-null-trap.rationale: Smudged banned-list entry maps NULL in NOT IN to an UNKNOWN that is never TRUE, contrasted with NOT EXISTS; limit (fixed three-valued rules; plain IN still TRUE on a match) accurate; a 'rule of three' wrong-sense link reworded.

asql-quantified-comparisons.rationale: ANY/ALL are explained as plain-English bullets with executed edge cases; an analogy would add nothing.

asql-subquery-plans.rationale: Plan-reading unit about EXPLAIN output and memory settings; a comparison would not clarify plan shapes.

asql-named-ctes.rationale: Naming intermediate results is already an everyday idea stated directly; no analogy needed.

asql-cte-planner.rationale: Made-to-order vs batch-cooked sauce maps inlining and materialisation; limit (version rules, MATERIALIZED / NOT MATERIALIZED overrides, rows read on demand) matches PG queries-with.

asql-recursive-steps.rationale: Phone-tree rounds map anchor, working table and the empty terminating pass; limit (UNION ALL keeps no memory of who was called, so cycles loop) accurate.

asql-recursive-hierarchies.rationale: The org-chart tree drawing is itself the familiar picture; another analogy would repeat it.

asql-recursive-series.rationale: Diary vs pre-printed register maps sparse orders, generated calendar, LEFT JOIN and COALESCE; limit (you choose the range; empty line is NULL until COALESCE) accurate.

asql-recursive-cycles.rationale: Chalk marks map a carried visited-path column and CYCLE; limit (per-path marks; distinct routes may revisit a node) accurate and consistent with executed path-check output.

asql-data-changing-ctes.rationale: Short dialect table and one snapshot rule; procedure-like content.

asql-window-aggregates.rationale: Summary sheet vs mark sheet maps GROUP BY vs a partitioned window aggregate; limit (ordered frames give each row a different set) accurate.

asql-window-ranking.rationale: Corrected: the author's 'finish-line camera still lists one of them first' contradicted a dead heat; now a results printout must list one name first (ROW_NUMBER), official shared places (RANK), distinct times (DENSE_RANK); limit notes the printer may choose a rule while ROW_NUMBER follows none, and that sporting conventions vary.

asql-window-top-per-group.rationale: A practical pattern continuing the ranking lesson, which carries the analogy.

asql-window-offsets.rationale: Previous diary page maps LAG reading the previous row, not the previous calendar day; limit (first page / default, ORDER BY defines previous) accurate.

asql-window-running-frames.rationale: End-of-day vs per-payment balance maps default RANGE peers vs ROWS; limit (SQL has no order among peers without a tie-breaker) accurate and matches the executed PG/SQLite tie swap.

asql-window-moving-frames.rationale: Builds on the running-frames analogy; the ROWS-vs-days caveat is stated directly.

asql-window-last-value.rationale: Short trap plus dialect and performance notes; the frame rule is better shown by the executed example.

asql-set-union.rationale: Stapled vs clean guest lists map UNION ALL, UNION, INTERSECT and EXCEPT; limit (whole-row positional matching, column names never compared) accurate.

asql-set-nulls-multiplicity.rationale: NULL distinctness and copy counts are precise rules best stated directly; the set-union lesson carries the analogy.

asql-set-precedence.rationale: Operator precedence is already compared to * binding tighter than +, a sufficient familiar reference.

asql-conditional-pivots.rationale: Department tally columns map conditional aggregates per GROUP BY group; limit (FILTER or CASE without ELSE gives NULL, not 0) accurate and executed.

asql-dynamic-unpivot.rationale: Report-shape and code-generation advice; no single mechanism benefits from a comparison.

asql-rollup-grouping.rationale: Itemised bill maps detail, per-person prefix subtotals and the empty grouping; limit (subtotal rows marked only by NULLs; GROUPING() distinguishes) accurate and executed.

asql-nth-highest.rationale: Interview probe list about ties and empty results; concrete numbers explain it better.

asql-top-group-strategies.rationale: Strategy comparison of SQL forms and index probes; an analogy would oversimplify the plan trade-offs.

asql-relational-division.rationale: Stamp card maps COUNT(DISTINCT) of required items; limit (hard-coded 2 must match the list; empty-list rule). Corrected: the COUNT-vs-DISTINCT pitfall the author had placed inside the callout is visible prose again.

asql-login-islands.rationale: Seat number minus own number maps date minus ROW_NUMBER; limit (two logins on one day break it, so deduplicate) accurate and also stated outside.

asql-revenue-thresholds.rationale: Short continuation of running totals; the threshold walk is concrete already.

asql-median-rows.rationale: The median is familiar; the content is about SQL forms and engine availability.

asql-outer-join-filters.rationale: The ON-vs-WHERE trap is shown directly with executed results; an analogy could blur the NULL-padding detail.

asql-json-storage.rationale: Photocopy vs typed record maps json vs jsonb; limit corrected because jsonb may rewrite how numbers and escapes are spelled (executed) and duplicate keys are dropped data rather than presentation.

asql-json-extraction.rationale: Operator/type reference; the hazards are concrete examples.

asql-json-array-rows.rationale: Function reference for expanding and building JSON; examples are clearer than a comparison.

asql-json-indexes.rationale: Chapter tab vs back-of-book index maps an expression index vs a GIN index; limit (operator-class support; planner may still scan) matches PG datatype-json and executed EXPLAIN output.

asql-atomic-upserts.rationale: One-line-per-name sheet with a single clerk maps the unique index and ON CONFLICT vs check-then-insert; limit refined from a two-session test: waits only on the same unfinished key; READ COMMITTED then inserts/updates, REPEATABLE READ can fail with a serialization failure.

asql-upsert-batch-replace.rationale: Correct-the-form vs shred-and-refile maps DO UPDATE vs INSERT OR REPLACE; limit kept short, with the trigger/cascade facts restored to visible prose (they had been moved inside the callout).

asql-merge-concurrency.rationale: MERGE clause order and version notes; the upsert analogy in asql-atomic-upserts already covers the concurrency idea.
